s: God's people have rebelled. He rejects empty worship, but promises: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be made white as snow.
In the last days all nations will stream to the Lord's mountain, and swords will be beaten into ploughshares. The proud will be humbled.
Judgment on Jerusalem's leaders and on its proud women.
Those who remain in Zion will be holy, sheltered by God's glory.
The song of the vineyard that yielded wild grapes. Woes against injustice.
Isaiah sees the Lord on his throne and the seraphim crying Holy, holy, holy. His lips are cleansed with a coal, and he answers, Here I am, send me.
Isaiah tells King Ahaz to trust God and gives a sign: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel.
Isaiah's son is a sign that Assyria will come. Trust the Lord, not the alliances of men.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light: a child is born to us, the Prince of Peace.
Woe to unjust lawmakers. Assyria is God's rod, but it too will be judged.
A shoot will come from the root of Jesse, filled with the Spirit of the Lord. The wolf will lie down with the lamb.
A song of thanks: draw water with joy from the springs of salvation.
God will punish Babylon on the day of the Lord.
Israel will be restored. A taunt over the fall of Babylon's king, the morning star cast down.
A lament over Moab's ruin.
Moab seeks refuge in Zion, and the prophet weeps for Moab.
Damascus and Israel will fall.
A message to Ethiopia: the nations will bring gifts to the Lord.
Egypt will be struck, but will then turn to the Lord and know him.
Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign that Egypt and Ethiopia will be taken captive.
Babylon has fallen. Oracles about Edom and Arabia.
Jerusalem revels instead of repenting. Shebna is replaced by Eliakim, who will hold the key of David.
Tyre, the great trading city, will be brought low.
The Lord will judge the whole earth.
God will make a feast for all peoples on his mountain and wipe away tears from every face.
A song of trust in the city of salvation. Your dead shall live.
God will slay the sea monster and gather his scattered people.
Woe to Ephraim's drunken leaders. God lays a precious cornerstone in Zion.
Woe to Jerusalem: its people honour God with their lips but their hearts are far from him.
Woe to those who trust in Egypt. In returning and rest you shall be saved.
Do not rely on Egypt's horses. The Lord will protect Jerusalem.
A king will reign in justice, and the Spirit will be poured out from on high.
The Lord is our judge and king; he will save us.
God's anger against the nations, especially Edom.
The desert will bloom. The eyes of the blind will be opened and the ransomed will return to Zion with joy.
Sennacherib's officer mocks Jerusalem's trust in God.
Hezekiah prays, and Isaiah says Assyria will not take the city. The angel of the Lord strikes the Assyrian camp.
Hezekiah is healed and the shadow on the sundial goes back. His song of thanks.
Hezekiah shows his treasures to Babylonian envoys, and Isaiah foretells exile to Babylon.
Comfort my people. A voice cries: prepare the way of the Lord in the desert. God feeds his flock like a shepherd.
God strengthens Israel against the nations. Idols can do nothing.
Behold my servant, in whom my soul delights: he will bring justice to the nations and be a light to them.
Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine. God will do a new thing.
God will pour out his Spirit. The folly of making a god from half a log.
God calls Cyrus his anointed to free his people. There is no other God.
The idols of Babylon must be carried, but God carries his people.
Babylon, the proud queen, will be humbled.
God refines Israel for his own sake and calls it out of Babylon.
The servant is called from the womb as a light to the nations. Can a mother forget her child? Yet I will not forget you.
The servant does not turn away from those who strike him, trusting God to help him.
God will comfort Zion. Awake and put on strength.
How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of one who brings good news. My servant will be exalted.
The suffering servant is despised and rejected, wounded for our sins. By his wounds we are healed.
Zion, once barren, will have many children. God's love will never depart from her.
Come to the waters, all who are thirsty. Seek the Lord while he may be found; his word will not return empty.
God's house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
God dwells with the humble and contrite.
The fast God wants: to free the oppressed and share bread with the hungry.
Israel's sins have separated them from God. The Redeemer will come to Zion.
Arise, shine, for your light has come. The nations will come to your light.
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, to bring good news to the poor and proclaim the year of the Lord's favour.
Zion will be called by a new name, God's delight.
God comes from Edom having trodden the winepress alone. A prayer recalling his mercies.
O that you would tear open the heavens and come down. We are the clay and you are the potter.
God answers: he will create new heavens and a new earth.
Heaven is God's throne. He will comfort Jerusalem like a mother, and all nations will see his glory.

6: Isaiah sees God's glory in the temple and feels unworthy. Once cleansed, he answers: Here I am, send me. The angels' song is sung at every Mass.
7: Isaiah gives a sign: a virgin will bear a son called Emmanuel, God with us. Matthew sees it fulfilled in the birth of Jesus.
9: The prophet foresees a royal child called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Prince of Peace. The Church reads this at Christmas.
11: A king from David's family will be filled with the Spirit of the Lord and bring justice and peace.
40: The second part of Isaiah opens with comfort for the exiles. The Gospels apply this voice in the desert to John the Baptist.
53: God's servant suffers for the sins of others and by his wounds we are healed. The Church reads this on Good Friday as a portrait of Christ's passion.
61: Jesus reads these words in the synagogue at Nazareth and says: today this scripture is fulfilled.
